'''Shelvin Bernard Mack Jr.''' (born April 22, 1990) is an American former professional [[basketball]] player who is an analyst for [[CBS Sports]]. He played eight seasons in the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA) for seven different teams. Mack played [[college basketball]] for the [[Butler Bulldogs men's basketball|Butler Bulldogs]], where he was a starter on consecutive Final Four teams in 2010 and 2011.

==High school career==
Mack attended [[Bryan Station High School]] in [[Lexington, Kentucky]].<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://247sports.com/Player/Shelvin-Mack-60424/high-school-105263/ |title=Shelvin Mack, Bryan Station , Shooting Guard |website=247Sports |language=en-US |access-date=April 3, 2020}}</ref> As a senior in 2007–08, he averaged 23.7 points, 7.7 rebounds, 7.5 assists, and 3.8 steals per game as he was named to the Lexington All-City team after leading the Defenders to a 30–3 record.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2010/03/31/sports/ncaabasketball/31mack.html |title=For Mack, Life Has Imitated Art Imitating Life |last=Thamel |first=Pete |author-link=Pete Thamel |date=March 30, 2010 |website=[[The New York Times]] |access-date=March 30, 2010}}</ref><ref name="bio">{{Cite web |url=http://www.butlersports.com/sports/m-baskbl/2010-11/bios/mack_shelvin00.html |title=1 – Shelvin Mack |website=ButlerSports.com |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140815185830/http://www.butlersports.com/sports/m-baskbl/2010-11/bios/mack_shelvin00.html |archive-date=August 15, 2014 |access-date=July 26, 2014}}</ref>

==College career==
In his freshman season at [[Butler Bulldogs men's basketball|Butler]], Mack started in all 32 games, sharing the Butler freshman record for games started with teammates [[Ronald Nored]] and future Jazz teammate [[Gordon Hayward]]. He was named to the Horizon League All-Newcomer team and the Horizon League All-Tournament team after leading the Bulldogs in assists in 2008–09, becoming just the third freshman in Butler history to record 100 assists. In 32 games, he averaged 11.9 points, 4.4 rebounds, 3.5 assists and 1.1 steals in 30.8 minutes per game.<ref name="bio" /><ref name="stats">{{Cite web |url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cbb/players/shelvin-mack-1.html |title=Shelvin Mack Stats |website=Sports-Reference.com |access-date=July 26, 2014}}</ref> During the off-season, Mack helped lead Team USA to the gold medal in the [[2009 FIBA Under-19 World Championship]] with averages of 5.9 points per game.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Katz |first=Andy |author-link=Andy Katz |date=July 13, 2009 |title=U.S. U-19 team captures first gold since 1991 |url=http://espn.go.com/mens-college-basketball/blog/_/name/katz_andy/id/4323444/us-u-19-team-captures-gold-new-zealand |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150111085017/http://espn.go.com/mens-college-basketball/blog/_/name/katz_andy/id/4323444/us-u-19-team-captures-gold-new-zealand |archive-date=January 11, 2015 |access-date=March 30, 2010 |website=ESPN.com}}</ref>

In his sophomore season, he was named to the All-Horizon League first team and the NABC All-District 12 first team. He was also named to the Horizon League All-Tournament team and the West Regional All-Tournament team. In 38 games (all starts), he averaged 14.1 points, 3.7 rebounds, 3.0 assists and 1.4 steals in 30.9 minutes per game.<ref name="bio" /><ref name="stats" /> He helped lead Butler to the 2010 National Championship game against Duke where Gordon Hayward missed a game-winning half-court shot which would have given Butler their very first NCAA championship.<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://usatoday30.usatoday.com/sports/college/mensbasketball/2010-04-06-butler-loses-sidebar_N.htm |title=Butler's would-be winning shot 'felt good' but fell short vs. Duke |last=Moore |first=David Leon |date=April 6, 2010 |website=USAToday.com |access-date=April 6, 2010}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |url=http://hangtime.blogs.nba.com/2016/02/21/morning-shootaround-feb-21-3/#stevens |title=MORNING SHOOTAROUND — FEB. 21 |date=February 21, 2016 |website=NBA.com |access-date=February 22, 2016}}</ref>

In his junior season, he was named to the All-Horizon League second team and the NABC All-District 12 second team. He became just the 33rd Butler player to score 1,000 career points. In 38 games (37 starts), he averaged 16.0 points, 4.5 rebounds and 3.4 assists in 32.1 minutes per game.<ref name="bio" /><ref name="stats" />

On April 21, 2011, he declared for the NBA draft, foregoing his final year of college eligibility.<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.butlersports.com/sports/m-baskbl/2010-11/releases/041211aaa |title=Shelvin Mack Declares For NBA Draft |date=April 21, 2011 |website=ButlerSports.com |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110501073506/http://www.butlersports.com/sports/m-baskbl/2010-11/releases/041211aaa |archive-date=May 1, 2011 |access-date=April 21, 2011}}</ref>

==Professional career==

===Washington Wizards (2011–2012)===
On June 23, 2011, Mack was selected with the 34th overall pick in the [[2011 NBA draft]] by the [[Washington Wizards]].<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.bulletsforever.com/2011/6/23/2240876/wizards-draft-results-Shelvin-Mack |title=Washington Wizards Select Shelvin Mack With No. 34 Pick In 2011 NBA Draft |date=June 24, 2011 |website=BulletsForever.com |publisher=SB Nation |access-date=June 24, 2011}}</ref> On December 9, 2011, he signed with the Wizards following the conclusion of the [[2011 NBA lockout|NBA lockout]]. On February 1, 2012, he scored a then career-high 12 points in a 109–103 loss to the [[Orlando Magic]].<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/blogs/wizards-insider/post/wizards-shelvin-mack-kevin-seraphin-have-career-nights-in-orlando/2012/02/02/gIQAJp3EkQ_blog.html |title=Wizards' Shelvin Mack, Kevin Seraphin have career nights in Orlando |last=Lee |first=Michael |date=February 2, 2012 |website=WashingtonPost.com |access-date=March 16, 2013}}</ref>

In July 2012, Mack joined the Washington Wizards for the 2012 NBA Summer League. On October 28, 2012, he was waived by the Wizards.<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.nba.com/wizards/news/wizards-waive-cook-and-mack |title=Wizards Waive Cook and Mack |date=October 28, 2012 |website=NBA.com |access-date=October 28, 2012}}</ref>

=== Maine Red Claws (2012) ===
On November 2, Mack was selected with the fourth overall pick in the [[2012 NBA Development League draft]] by the [[Maine Red Claws]].<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.nba.com/dleague/maine/draft_2012.html |title=RED CLAWS SELECT SHELVIN MACK IN FIRST ROUND OF NBADL DRAFT |date=November 2, 2012 |website=NBA.com |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150218004314/http://www.nba.com/dleague/maine/draft_2012.html |archive-date=February 18, 2015 |access-date=November 2, 2012}}</ref>

=== Return to Washington (2012–2013) ===
On December 25, 2012, Mack re-signed with the Wizards,<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.nba.com/wizards/news/wizards-sign-shelvin-mack-and-garrett-temple |title=Wizards Sign Shelvin Mack And Garrett Temple |date=December 25, 2012 |website=NBA.com |access-date=December 25, 2012}}</ref> but was again waived by the team on January 7, 2013.<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.nba.com/wizards/wizards-waive-shelvin-mack |title=Wizards Waive Shelvin Mack |date=January 7, 2013 |website=NBA.com |access-date=January 7, 2013}}</ref>

=== Return to Maine (2013) ===
On January 9, 2013, Mack was reacquired by the Red Claws.<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.nba.com/dleague/maine/transaction_010913.html |title=SHELVIN MACK REJOINS RED CLAWS |date=January 9, 2013 |website=NBA.com |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140811054242/http://www.nba.com/dleague/maine/transaction_010913.html |archive-date=August 11, 2014 |access-date=January 9, 2013}}</ref>

=== Philadelphia 76ers (2013) ===
On January 17, 2013, Mack signed a 10-day contract with the [[Philadelphia 76ers]].<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.nba.com/sixers/news/sixers-sign-guard-shelvin-mack-10-day-contract |title=Sixers Sign Guard Shelvin Mack to 10-Day Contract |date=January 17, 2013 |website=NBA.com |access-date=January 17, 2013}}</ref> On January 28, he signed a second 10-day contract with the 76ers.<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.nba.com/sixers/news/130128-shelvin-mack |title=Sixers Sign Guard Shelvin Mack To Second 10-day Contract |date=January 28, 2013 |website=NBA.com |access-date=January 28, 2013}}</ref> He was not retained by the 76ers following his second 10-day contract,

=== Third stint with Maine (2013) ===
On February 7, 2013, Mack was reacquired by the Red Claws. He went on to play for the Futures All-Star team in the 2013 NBA D-League All-Star Game.<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.nba.com/dleague/news/2013_nba_development_league_all_star_rosters_announced_2013_02_04.html |title=2013 NBA Development League All-Star Game Rosters Announced |date=February 4, 2013 |website=NBA.com |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160812091051/http://www.nba.com/dleague/news/2013_nba_development_league_all_star_rosters_announced_2013_02_04.html |archive-date=August 12, 2016 |access-date=February 4, 2013}}</ref>

===Atlanta Hawks (2013–2016)===
[[File:Shelvin Mack Hawks.jpg|thumb|Mack with the [[Atlanta Hawks]] in November 2013]]
On March 6, 2013, Mack signed a 10-day contract with the [[Atlanta Hawks]].<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.nba.com/hawks/news/atlanta-hawks-sign-shelvin-mack-10-day-contract |title=ATLANTA HAWKS SIGN SHELVIN MACK TO 10-DAY CONTRACT |date=March 6, 2013 |website=NBA.com |access-date=March 6, 2013}}</ref> On March 16, he signed a second 10-day contract.<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.nba.com/hawks/news/atlanta-hawks-sign-shelvin-mack-second-10-day-contract |title=ATLANTA HAWKS SIGN SHELVIN MACK TO SECOND 10-DAY CONTRACT |date=March 16, 2013 |website=NBA.com |access-date=March 16, 2013}}</ref> On March 26, he signed a two-year, non-guaranteed deal with the Hawks.<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.nba.com/hawks/news/atlanta-hawks-sign-shelvin-mack-remainder-season |title=ATLANTA HAWKS SIGN SHELVIN MACK FOR REMAINDER OF THE SEASON |date=March 26, 2013 |website=NBA.com |access-date=March 26, 2013}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.nba.com/hawks/features/shelvin-mack-finally-right-place |title=Mack finally finds home |last=Cooper |first=Jon |date=April 8, 2013 |website=NBA.com |access-date=April 8, 2013}}</ref>

In July 2013, Mack joined the Hawks for the [[2013 NBA Summer League]]. On February 21, 2014, he scored a then career-high 21 points in a 115–107 loss to the [[Detroit Pistons]].<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.nba.com/games/20140221/ATLDET/gameinfo.html |title=Notebook: Pistons 115, Hawks 107 |date=February 21, 2014 |website=NBA.com |access-date=February 21, 2014}}</ref> In 2013–14, he played 73 games, averaging 7.5 points, 2.2 rebounds and 1.7 assists per game.

On August 22, 2014, Mack re-signed with the Hawks to a three-year, $7.3 million contract.<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.nba.com/hawks/news/hawks-re-sign-shelvin-mack |title=Hawks Re-Sign Shelvin Mack |date=August 22, 2014 |website=NBA.com |access-date=August 22, 2014}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Wojnarowski |first=Adrian |author-link=Adrian Wojnarowski |date=July 25, 2014 |title=Shelvin Mack Agrees To Three-Year, $7.3M Deal With Hawks |url=http://basketball.realgm.com/wiretap/234425/Shelvin-Mack-Agrees-To-Three-Year-$73M-Deal-With-Hawks |access-date=July 26, 2014 |website=RealGM.com}}</ref> On December 17, 2014, he scored a career-high 24 points on 6-of-6 from three-point range off the bench in a 127–98 win over the [[Cleveland Cavaliers]].<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.nba.com/games/20141217/ATLCLE/gameinfo.html |title=Mack leads surging Hawks to blowout in Cleveland |date=December 17, 2014 |website=NBA.com |access-date=December 17, 2014}}</ref>

===Utah Jazz (2016–2017)===
On February 18, 2016, Mack was traded to the [[Utah Jazz]] in a three-team trade involving the Hawks and the [[Chicago Bulls]].<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.nba.com/jazz/news/jazz-acquire-shelvin-mack-atlanta |title=Jazz Acquire Shelvin Mack from Atlanta |date=February 18, 2016 |website=NBA.com |access-date=February 18, 2016}}</ref> The move reunited him with former Butler teammate [[Gordon Hayward]] and former Hawks assistant [[Quin Snyder]]. He made his debut for the Jazz on February 21, recording a season-high 16 points and six assists off the bench in a 115–111 loss to the [[Portland Trail Blazers]].<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.nba.com/games/20160221/UTAPOR/gameinfo.html |title=McCollum scores 31 as Trail Blazers edge Jazz 115-111 |date=February 21, 2016 |website=NBA.com |access-date=February 22, 2016}}</ref> In the Jazz's next game two days later, Mack was elevated to the starting point guard role, replacing [[Raul Neto]]. He subsequently topped his season-high with 17 points in 32 minutes of action, as the Jazz defeated the [[Houston Rockets]] 117–114 in overtime.<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.nba.com/games/20160223/HOUUTA/gameinfo.html |title=Hayward scores 28 as Jazz defeat Rockets 117-114 in overtime |date=February 23, 2016 |website=NBA.com |access-date=February 23, 2016}}</ref> On March 11, he scored a career-high 27 points in a 114–93 win over the Washington Wizards.<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.nba.com/games/20160311/WASUTA/gameinfo.html |title=Mack scores career-high 27 as Jazz beat Wizards 114-93 |date=March 11, 2016 |website=NBA.com |access-date=March 11, 2016}}</ref>

On December 8, 2016, Mack scored a season-high 19 points in a 106–99 loss to the [[Golden State Warriors]].<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400899777 |title=Curry scores 26, Warriors beat Jazz 106-99 |date=December 8, 2016 |website=ESPN.com |access-date=December 9, 2016 |agency=Associated Press}}</ref>

===Orlando Magic (2017–2018)===
On July 9, 2017, Mack signed with the [[Orlando Magic]].<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.nba.com/magic/news/orlando-magic-sign-shelvin-mack |title=Orlando Magic Sign Shelvin Mack |date=July 9, 2017 |website=NBA.com |access-date=July 9, 2017}}</ref> In the [[2017-18 NBA season]], Mack led the Orlando Magic in assists, with 3.9 per game.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://fansided.com/2018/04/23/congratulations-shelvin-mack-3-9-assists/ |title=Congratulations to Shelvin Mack and his 3.9 assists per game! |date=April 23, 2018 |website=fansided.com |access-date=January 14, 2021}}</ref> On June 25, 2018, he was waived by the Magic.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.nba.com/magic/news/magic-waive-shelvin-mack |title=Magic Waive Shelvin Mack |last=Denton |first=John |date=June 25, 2018 |website=NBA.com |access-date=July 9, 2018}}</ref>

===Memphis Grizzlies (2018–2019)===
On August 7, 2018, Mack signed with the [[Memphis Grizzlies]].<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.nba.com/grizzlies/news/grizzlies-sign-shelvin-mack-180807 |title=Grizzlies sign Shelvin Mack |date=August 7, 2018 |website=NBA.com |access-date=August 7, 2018}}</ref>

On February 7, 2019, Mack was traded to the [[Atlanta Hawks]] in exchange for [[Tyler Dorsey]].<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.nba.com/grizzlies/memphis-grizzlies-acquire-tyler-dorsey-atlanta-hawks |title=Memphis Grizzlies acquire Tyler Dorsey from Atlanta Hawks |date=February 7, 2019 |website=NBA.com |access-date=February 7, 2019}}</ref> He was waived by the Hawks the following day.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.nba.com/hawks/atlanta-hawks-request-waivers-shelvin-mack |title=Atlanta Hawks Request Waivers On Shelvin Mack |date=February 8, 2019 |website=NBA.com |access-date=February 8, 2019}}</ref>

===Charlotte Hornets (2019)===
On February 10, 2019, Mack was claimed off waivers by the [[Charlotte Hornets]].<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.nba.com/hornets/press-releases/hornets-awarded-shelvin-mack-waiver-claim |title=Hornets Awarded Shelvin Mack On Waiver Claim |last=Wash |first=Quinton |date=February 10, 2019 |website=NBA.com |access-date=February 10, 2019}}</ref>

===Olimpia Milano (2019–2020)===
On July 25, 2019, Mack signed a two-year deal with [[Pallacanestro Olimpia Milano|Olimpia Milano]] of the Italian [[Lega Basket Serie A]] and the [[EuroLeague]].<ref>{{Cite news |url=https://www.euroleague.net/news/i/9tosesbcwmxiip7q/milan-lands-veteran-guard-mack |title=Milan lands veteran guard Mack |date=July 25, 2019 |work=EuroLeague.net |access-date=July 25, 2019}}</ref> He appeared in 19 games for Milano, averaging 5.8 points, 2.4 rebounds, and 2.4 assists in 18 minutes per game.

=== Hapoel Jerusalem (2020) ===
On January 16, 2020, Mack parted ways with Milano to join [[Hapoel Jerusalem B.C.|Hapoel Jerusalem]] of the [[Israeli Basketball Premier League|Israeli Premier League]] for the rest of the season.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Skerlatic |first=Dario |url=https://sportando.basketball/en/shelvin-mack-joins-hapoel-jerusalem/ |title=Shelvin Mack joins Hapoel Jerusalem |date=January 16, 2020 |work=Sportando |access-date=January 16, 2020}}</ref>

=== Panathinaikos (2020–2021) ===
On November 7, 2020, Mack signed a two-month deal with European powerhouse [[Panathinaikos B.C.|Panathinaikos]] of the [[Greek Basket League]] and the [[EuroLeague]].<ref>{{Cite news |last=Borghesan |first=Ennio Terrasi |date=2020-11-07 |title=Panathinaikos officially announces signing of Shelvin Mack - Sportando |url=https://sportando.basketball/en/panathinaikos-officially-announces-signing-of-shelvin-mack/ |access-date=2024-03-22 |website=Sportando |language=en-US}}</ref> His contract was subsequently renewed for the rest of the 2020–2021 season. On June 6, 2021, Mack parted ways with the Greek club amidst the [[Greek Basket League|domestic competition]] finals against [[Lavrio B.C.|Lavrio]] in order to attend to personal matters overseas. In 23 [[Greek Basket League|GBL]] and 21 [[EuroLeague]] games with the Greens, Mack averaged 6.5 points, 2 rebounds, and 4 assists.

== Broadcasting ==
In March 2022, Mack provided coverage for the [[2022 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=CBS SPORTS NETWORK TO DELIVER COMPREHENSIVE COVERAGE THROUGHOUT 2022 NCAA DIVISION I MEN'S BASKETBALL CHAMPIONSHIP |url=https://www.paramountpressexpress.com/cbs-sports/shows/college-basketball/releases/?view=59319-cbs-sports-network-to-deliver-comprehensive-coverage-throughout-2022-ncaa-division-i-mens-basketball-championship |access-date=February 24, 2023 |website=Paramount| date=March 10, 2022 }}</ref> He is currently an analyst for the [[CBS Sports]] show ''Inside College Basketball''.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Inside College Basketball: What to Expect from UNC on Thanksgiving Day |url=https://www.cbssports.com/college-basketball/video/inside-college-basketball-what-to-expect-from-unc-on-thanksgiving-day/ |access-date=February 24, 2023 |website=CBS Sports}}</ref>
